html:
SMTO-LLM-0103 — SMTO couldn't prepare this image for the model

GUID: 7deef957-3f5b-5da3-b6a8-2b98e82586c9
Slug: vision-input-error
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: vision

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't open the picture, or it was too large to send, so the image model never saw it. Your file wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Save the picture as a PNG or JPEG (for example with Save As in an image app, or by taking a screenshot of it), then add it again with Add context. SMTO can only read PNG and JPEG pictures, and damaged or other file types fail this check.
  2. If the picture is very large, shrink or crop it to the part you need, keeping it under 4 MB. SMTO refuses pictures that are too big in file size or in pixel dimensions.
  3. For a PDF, ask about one or two pages at a time. Pages are turned into pictures for the model, and several large pages can go over the size limit together.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's reply describes the picture or page you asked about.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the picture if you are allowed to share it, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat the picture as reviewed; the model never saw it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Vision tool rejected the image before the model request (vision_input_error fallback for a ScreenError or client error without a more specific kind): the input was not a decodable PNG/JPEG, exceeded a byte or pixel limit, or could not be re-encoded.

What this means

  • The shared image validator rejected the image before a usable observation was produced. The retained image-validation reason determines the supported correction. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The shared image validator rejected the image before a usable observation was produced. The retained image-validation reason determines the supported correction.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • Read the tool result message for the specific validation reason. Supply a valid PNG or JPEG within the decode byte and pixel limits (the re-encoded image input is also capped at 4 MiB per call), or re-render PDF pages at lower resolution or fewer pages per call.
  • Use a valid supported PNG/JPEG image or render the selected PDF page again within the size and decoding limits.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Image validation completes and the bounded image request reaches the selected capable model.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
